grade_reason: His only statement of his own on AI risk found (17 September 2026) calls for 'legitimate real AI safety' without describing a catastrophic or serious danger from AI, so it is D, on the boundary with C. His other AI material is press releases on AI education and workforce funding.
notes: Seven web searches ran; none was refused. The quote comes from a secondary news report (The Next Web), not a transcript; the same article also quotes him: 'Retreating and failing is not an option in this area' and 'It's on us now to chart a course moving forward.' A reviewer may consider C, since he spoke at an event framed around AI as a serious threat, but the serious-threat wording ('a true threat to a global existence') was Katherine Clark's, not his. Many of his aguilar.house.gov press releases (2025 and 2026) announce federal money for AI education, workforce and research in the Inland Empire (for example https://aguilar.house.gov/2026/08/31/rep-aguilar-sen-schiff-deliver-more-than-1-million-for-cal-state-san-bernardino-ai-research-center/); these were seen only in search results, not opened, and are level D at most. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, Casar): no source found shows Aguilar as a sponsor or cosponsor, but the full cosponsor list was not checked on Congress.gov. As a member of Democratic leadership he may have signed the 16 September 2026 letter to Speaker Johnson; per instructions that letter was not searched and is left to the central build. No other House letter about AI risk signed or led by him was found.
